hero.heading: Academic environment for real life.
hero.subtext: We built Polyglot International School in Samarkand around three main priorities of parents: strong education, absolute safety, and the right life values for children.
hero.heading2: A place where every child's potential comes to life.
hero.subtext2: A modern campus, caring teachers, and a supportive atmosphere help children grow confident and curious.
hero.heading3: The future begins with the right choice of school.
hero.subtext3: International learning standards and genuine care for every student are at the heart of everything we do at Polyglot International School.

certificates.heading: International certificates without tutors
certificates.body: We guide every student to clear, measurable academic results recognised worldwide. The programme is built so that preparation for international exams becomes a natural part of everyday study.
certificates.bodyExtra: No evening tutors, no weekends buried in textbooks. Language modules, academic writing and mathematics are woven into the schedule — a child arrives at the exam fully prepared, without overload or stress.
certificates.item1: Direct preparation for IELTS (target 7.0+), SAT (1400+) and HSK (Chinese language).
certificates.item2: Official exams are taken directly at school, in a calm environment for the child.
certificates.item3: Personalised tracks: difficulty adapts to each individual student.
certificates.item4: Transparent progress analytics — parents see results in real time.

features.heading: Readiness for business and adult life.
features.subtext: The school doesn't isolate a child from society — it develops practical independence and social intelligence.
features.card1Body: Weekly meetings and networking with active entrepreneurs and top managers.
features.card2Body: Financial literacy, marketing, podcast creation and public speaking.
features.card3Body: Etiquette, cultural behavior and communication in any environment.

friday-talk.label: Friday Talk
friday-talk.heading: Friday Talk: live networking with real leaders
friday-talk.intro: Every Friday, classes pause for an hour — not for a break, but to meet the real world. An entrepreneur, top executive, or public figure comes to the assembly hall ready to speak with students as equals.

points.title: Guests from real business
points.body: Over 30 speakers come through Friday Talk each year — from startup founders to executives of major Uzbek companies.

points.title: No-script format
points.body: 30 minutes of talk, then open questions from students — no moderation, no prepared answers.

points.title: Networking afterwards
points.body: After every session, informal conversation, contact exchange, and sometimes internship invitations follow.

points.title: Logged in the portfolio
points.body: Every meeting is recorded in the student's personal portfolio as part of their extracurricular record.

practical-skills.label: Practical Skills
practical-skills.heading: Practical skills: from theory to real application
practical-skills.intro: Knowledge becomes a skill only when it is applied. The practical skills track is built around real tools students use from their very first lessons.

points.title: Financial literacy
points.body: Personal budgeting, investment basics, taxes and credit — explained with real life examples, not abstract problems.

points.title: Marketing & SMM
points.body: Students run training projects on social media, analyse real brand cases and build their own mini campaigns.

points.title: Podcast creation
points.body: Recording, editing and promoting their own audio show in the school's equipped media studio.

points.title: Public speaking
points.body: Regular practice speaking in front of an audience — from classroom presentations to the Friday Talk stage.

culture.label: Culture
culture.heading: Culture: confidence in any setting
culture.intro: Academic success means little without the ability to carry oneself with dignity in any situation. The culture track prepares students for business, social and international communication.

points.title: Business & social etiquette
points.body: Table manners, dress code, norms of business communication — things usually learned only in adult life.

points.title: Cross-cultural communication
points.body: Practice communicating with people from different cultures through the school's language clubs and international programmes.

points.title: Confident speech
points.body: Voice training, diction and argumentation — the foundation of confident communication in any professional setting.

points.title: Empathy & tact
points.body: Developing social intelligence through role play and analysis of real communication situations.

campus.body: We built the campus around the question: «What should surround a child so that 11 years at school become a time of growth, not survival?» Earthquake-resistant construction, individual transport, laboratories for real experiments — these aren't features, they're basic environmental hygiene.

aboutPage.label: Manifesto
aboutPage.heading: Three Fundamental Standards of Polyglot
aboutPage.intro: When choosing a school, parents often focus on reputation, cost or proximity. We offer a different criterion — the long-term social capital of your child. Polyglot is built around three verifiable, measurable standards.
aboutPage.s1Body: International exams — IELTS, SAT, HSK — are embedded in the curriculum, not added at the end. Each student follows a personalised trajectory tracked by parents in real time.
aboutPage.s2Body: Safety is not just a guard at the entrance. It is engineering solutions, digital transparency and a system where parents know where their child is at every moment of the day.
aboutPage.s2d3: Real-time transfer geolocation via SCHOOL APP
aboutPage.s2d4: IQAir air quality monitoring in every classroom
aboutPage.s3Body: The school prepares not for tests but for life. Every academic block has application beyond the classroom — from the first lesson to the last day before university admission.
aboutPage.s3d1: Friday Talk — weekly networking with top managers
aboutPage.s3d2: Digital skills: Python, SMM, digital marketing
aboutPage.s3d3: Annual internships to the UK, Canada and the EU
aboutPage.s3d4: Entrepreneurship and personal brand from Grade 9
aboutPage.closing: Polyglot is not just a school. It is an investment in the long-term social capital of your child, which starts working from day one.

campusPage.heading: 12,000 m² of Earthquake-Resistant Infrastructure
campusPage.subheading: Five floors. One campus. An environment for growth.
campusPage.body: We built the campus asking one question: what should surround a child so that 11 years at school become a time of growth, not survival? Every engineering decision is an answer to that question.
campusPage.secBody: The building is designed so that unauthorised entry is physically impossible and every movement inside is recorded.
campusPage.sec2: Professional security on duty around the clock

campusPage.sec5: Transfer geolocation for every route via SCHOOL APP

campusPage.space2Desc: Virtual reality for interactive learning and simulations
campusPage.space3Desc: Workshop for programming and assembling robots
campusPage.space4Desc: Podcast recording, video projects and multimedia
campusPage.space5Desc: Full-size pitch and sports hall for physical development
campusPage.space6Desc: Venue for Friday Talk, presentations and public speaking

challengesPage.label: The Challenge
challengesPage.heading: Bridging the gap between academic theory and global market demands
challengesPage.intro: The global education system is facing a systemic crisis. The traditional school model, developed in the 19th century, is increasingly at odds with what the 21st century demands from young professionals.
challengesPage.stat1Label: of employers are dissatisfied with the practical preparation of graduates
challengesPage.stat2Label: increase in school burnout among students over the past 8 years
challengesPage.stat3Label: children need private tutors to pass international exams
challengesPage.p1Body: Traditional schools accumulate knowledge but do not build application skills. A graduate knows Ohm's Law in theory but cannot build a business model or deliver a public presentation.
challengesPage.p2Body: High academic pressure undermines mental and physical health before the first result is achieved. 6–8 hours at school, then tutors — this is not education, it is survival.
challengesPage.p3Body: Schools exist in a vacuum: no meetings with entrepreneurs, no international practice, no understanding of the labour market a child will serve in just 7–10 years.
challengesPage.sol1: International exams are integrated into the curriculum — no tutors needed
challengesPage.sol2: The school day is designed to prevent overload
challengesPage.sol3: Weekly Friday Talk — meetings with real professionals
challengesPage.sol4: Annual overseas internships from the first year of senior school

healthPage.label: Health & Logistics
healthPage.heading: Technological control of students' physical wellbeing
healthPage.intro: A child's safety does not end at the building perimeter. It includes the air quality they breathe, the food they eat, and the route they take home.
healthPage.airBody: Every classroom is fitted with air purifiers and sensors certified to the international IQAir standard. The system operates in real time and automatically responds to air quality changes.
healthPage.airFact1: Monitoring of CO₂, PM2.5, temperature and humidity
healthPage.airFact2: Automatic alert when norms are exceeded
healthPage.airFact4: Air quality data available in SCHOOL APP
healthPage.foodBody: Menus are designed by nutritionists specifically for school-age physiology, accounting for age-appropriate needs for proteins, carbohydrates and micronutrients. Buffet format — variety without compulsion.
healthPage.foodFact1: Breakfast, lunch and afternoon snack daily
healthPage.foodFact2: Menus planned by nutritionists a week in advance
healthPage.foodFact4: Daily menu published in SCHOOL APP
healthPage.transferBody: Every student is delivered from home to school and back on a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a verified professional driver. Parents see the route in real time.
healthPage.transferFact1: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter — comfortable and safe minibuses
healthPage.transferFact3: Real-time GPS tracking via SCHOOL APP

appPage.label: Digital Ecosystem
appPage.heading: SCHOOL APP: Absolute Transparency
appPage.subheading: One phone — complete control over your child's safety and progress
appPage.intro: Polyglot parents don't wait for the end of term to learn about their child's achievements. They know everything in real time — from a test score to the exact location of the school bus.
appPage.f1Body: The map with the real position of the school bus updates every 30 seconds. You see when the bus departed, where it is now and how many minutes until arrival.
appPage.f1detail2: Notification when the child boards and alights
appPage.f2Body: Grades, attendance, subject dynamics and teacher comments — all in one place. You see not just scores, but the trend: improving or declining.
appPage.f2detail1: Grades appear on the day they are entered
appPage.f2detail3: Attendance with the reason for absence
appPage.f3Body: The daily menu with dish composition, calories and allergens is published each morning. You know what your child ate before they get home.
appPage.f3detail3: Notification with the new menu every morning
appPage.f4Body: Chat with the homeroom teacher, administration and subject teachers — no intermediaries. All messages are delivered directly and logged in the system.
appPage.f4detail3: Book a meeting with a teacher online
appPage.f5Body: Push notifications for important events: schedule changes, events, test results and payment reminders — timely and without unnecessary noise.

educationPage.label: School Day
educationPage.heading: Synchronising the national standard with international programmes
educationPage.intro: The school day is engineered to maximise peak concentration hours and prevent overload. Academic work in the first half. Creativity and practice in the second.
educationPage.morningBody: The national curriculum and international disciplines alternate in the first half of the day, when concentration peaks. IELTS and SAT preparation is organically embedded — students engage with English in academic writing and analysis, not from separate textbooks.
educationPage.afternoonBody: After lunch the brain switches to creativity, physical activity and applied skills. Clubs, workshops and activities are not an addition to the programme — they are an organic part of it.
educationPage.techBody: The campus infrastructure enables real research, not just reading about it.
educationPage.tech1Desc: Physics, chemistry, biology — real experiments, not demonstrations
educationPage.tech2Desc: Virtual reality for geography, history and physics
educationPage.tech4Desc: Podcast recording, video projects and school media

gradesPage.label: Educational Trajectory
gradesPage.heading: From Grade 1 to admission to TOP-100 universities
gradesPage.intro: Each age stage has its own pedagogical priorities. The programme is structured as an ascending spiral: the skills of Grade 1 become the foundation of Grade 11.
gradesPage.pHeading: Continuity of stages: adaptation and cognitive development
gradesPage.pBody: The first four years are the foundation. We do not rush children: a gentle entry into learning through play and practice builds stable cognitive patterns and a love of knowledge without fear of failure.
gradesPage.pPhilosophy: Spatial thinking, fine motor skills and coordination are the foundation of mathematical and engineering thinking in the future.
gradesPage.pOutcome: A confident start in academic and physical activities, developed fine motor skills, basic language skills and an intrinsic motivation to learn.
gradesPage.mBody: Grades 5–8 are the time for first serious projects and professional tools. Emphasis on interdisciplinary learning: no subject exists in isolation. IT components, media literacy and etiquette build a well-rounded personality.
gradesPage.mPhilosophy: Algorithmic thinking is not just about programming. It is the skill of breaking down a problem — and that works in any profession.
gradesPage.mOutcome: First completed projects, confident speech in Russian and English, understanding of IT tools and critical evaluation of information.
gradesPage.sBody: Grades 9–11 transform a student into a specialist. Applied business disciplines, intensive IELTS/SAT preparation and personal brand work prepare students for admission to leading world universities.
gradesPage.sPhilosophy: By Grade 11 a Polyglot graduate arrives not just with a certificate but with a portfolio, international qualifications and a clear professional path.
gradesPage.sOutcome: Ready for TOP-100 university admission: international certificates, a formed portfolio, a personal brand and professional communication skills.

resultsPage.label: Academic Results
resultsPage.heading: Standardised metrics of academic achievement
resultsPage.intro: Polyglot does not use tutors as a system crutch. International exams are the natural result of a well-built curriculum, not an additional burden.
resultsPage.ieltsBody: Language modules, academic writing and oral communication are embedded in the daily schedule from Grade 5. Students arrive at the exam organically prepared — without evening sessions or stress.
resultsPage.ielts1: Daily reading and writing practice in English
resultsPage.ielts2: Academic writing as part of regular lessons
resultsPage.ielts3: Official exam taken at school, in a familiar environment
resultsPage.satBody: Mathematics and critical thinking at SAT level are embedded in the academic block. Text analysis, data work and algebra are taught with an international standards focus from Grade 7.
resultsPage.hskBody: Chinese is taught by native speakers from Grade 1. By Grade 9, students reach HSK 4, enabling free communication in a business environment — a strategic competitive advantage in the global market.
resultsPage.hsk2: Classes from Grade 1 with a systematic programme
resultsPage.hsk3: HSK 4 by the end of Grade 9
resultsPage.method1: International exam preparation is built into the main schedule
resultsPage.method2: Personalised trajectories adapt difficulty to each student
resultsPage.method3: Transparent analytics allow weak points to be addressed in time
resultsPage.method4: International-level teachers — no outsourcing to tutors

consultingPage.label: Polyglot Consulting
consultingPage.heading: A guaranteed track into the world's TOP-100 universities
consultingPage.intro: Admission to leading world universities is not a lottery — it is a managed process. The Polyglot Consulting Department accompanies every student from Grade 1 to the moment of enrolment.
consultingPage.step1Body: Identifying direction, interests and strengths via testing and individual sessions with a consultant.
consultingPage.step2Body: Systematic accumulation of academic and extracurricular achievements, projects, volunteering and awards from Year 1.
consultingPage.step3Body: Analysing universities by criteria: subject, ranking, cost, admission chances. Building a short list of 8–12 universities.
consultingPage.step4Body: Writing motivation letters, gathering recommendations, notarised translation of documents. Full support on all application platforms.
consultingPage.step5Body: Support at the offer acceptance stage, visa assistance, student accommodation and overseas adaptation.
consultingPage.r1: United Kingdom: UCL, King's College, Edinburgh

lifePage.heading: Social capital and international practical activity
lifePage.intro: The school does not isolate a child from the real world — it becomes their guide into it. Contact with professionals, international internships and cultural exchange shape a personality ready for a global environment.
lifePage.ftBody: Every Friday the Polyglot hall hosts a guest speaker — an entrepreneur, top manager, government official or scientist. Format: 30-minute address, student Q&A, informal networking.
lifePage.ft4: Graduates of international universities — role models

lifePage.comp2: International debate clubs and Model UN
